look_here_first: Ignore flower color at first. Check the woody shrub habit, opposite rough leaves, and stems: Texas lantana is a winter-deciduous, non-spinescent shrub with stiff-hairy/scabrous 4-sided young stems and coarse serrate leaves. Then inspect the flower-head bracts and confirm the axillary pedunculate head.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: winter-deciduous aromatic shrub, commonly around 0.5–1 m in regional treatments

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: young stems four-sided, stiff-hairy/scabrous, aging woody

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaves opposite and decussate, broadly ovate to ovate, short-petiolate

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaf blades rough/cobblestone-textured above with stiff hairs and strongly raised veins below

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: dense axillary flower heads borne on distinct peduncles

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: flowers commonly open yellow and age through orange to red, but color is secondary to vegetative/bract characters

lookalikes.differences: Lantana camara: A common non-native/invasive landscape escape. L. camara often has small prickles on the square stems and commonly larger leaves. Use inflorescence-bract structure and stem armature rather than flower color alone; absence of prickles by itself is not enough for a final ID. Lantana achyranthifolia: Native desert lantana has much more slender branches, narrower hairy leaves, and typically white-to-pink flowers with yellow centers rather than the robust broad-leaved Texas-lantana look. Lantana montevidensis: A common cultivated trailing lantana; habit is low/trailing rather than an upright woody Texas-lantana shrub, and flowers are usually lavender-purple.
